stories.title: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
stories.reason: First real measurement (not just compliance-checking) of MCP tool poisoning across 12 frameworks x 18 models x 45 scenarios with a public tool (mcpvenom); exact fit for 'agent/MCP attack chains' with a primary source and running code.
key_facts: 9,720-cell matrix: 12 frameworks, 18 models, 45 attack scenarios
Overall ASR 22.9% (2,113/9,720 vulnerable cells); 12.1% of vulnerable cells verifiably exfiltrate a secret via canary HTTP receipt
Model ASR ranges 0.4%-49.7%; Claude Opus 4.8 vulnerable in 8/530 cells with 223 explicit refusals
Code audit found no intentional defense in any of the 12 frameworks; all 5 coordinated vendor disclosures were rejected
Regex metadata scanner rejects 20/45 scenarios but at 7.2% false-positive rate

stories.title: WTF Ubuntu?
stories.reason: CVE-2026-98432 (CVSS 9.8, remote root, Linux TCP code since 2016) has a working exploit and Debian/Arch/Alpine patched it two+ weeks ago -- Ubuntu LTS is still vulnerable. Same underlying flaw Claude was reported to have exploited; ongoing real-world risk, not a rehash of the earlier 'Claude wrote the exploit' story.
key_facts: Debian patched Oct 16; Ubuntu had no patch as of Nov 2 14:48 UTC, 2+ weeks later
All supported Ubuntu releases incl. LTS listed vulnerable
Arch and Alpine (volunteer-run distros) already fixed
Red Hat 8/9/10 patched; Ubuntu's fix sits in opt-in testing channel with no ship date

stories.title: Postman silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data
stories.reason: Postman silently installed Claude Code/Codex/CLI plugins and a startup hook pushing its skill into unrelated API work on upgrade; no confirmed data exfiltration but a real agent-supply-chain trust failure (self-approving hooks).
key_facts: Upgrade from 12.33.4 auto-installed claude-code and codex plugins (source: auto-existing-upgrade)
SessionStart hook pushes 'postman:api-engineer' skill for any non-trivial API task
Installer calls approvePostmanHook() to self-write trust records into hooks.state
Postman says bundling 'eased setup' and will make opt-in clearer; reviewing hook approval
No confirmed data exfiltration -- only the remote MCP endpoint and startup instruction were documented

stories.title: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency
stories.reason: CWE-bench v2 is exactly the kind of security benchmark Mine flags to always-surface: open dataset+grader+leaderboard, real agent-vs-repo-fix task, with concrete pass@1/cost numbers across 11 models.
key_facts: 100 public tasks across 91 CWEs, Harbor-packaged, hand-reviewed, held-out eval set available on request
Dataset/grader/harness open on Hugging Face (collinear-ai/cwe-bench) with a public leaderboard
Gemini 4 Argon leads: 67.8% pass@1 / 81.0% pass@4; Claude Opus 5.5: 67.3% / 78.0%
Even the leader fails 19% of tasks on every attempt; 95/100 tasks solved by at least one model
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash hits 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04/rollout vs Opus $1.83 and Gemini $3.92

stories.title: Google Warns LLMjacking Attacks Are Costing Some Enterprises Up to $1 Million in Cloud Charges
stories.reason: Google's LLMjacking warning gives hard numbers on a real, growing AI-infra attack class (stolen API keys monetized via resale 'LLM Mixers'), with named CVE and TTPs -- strong AI x cyber discovery.
key_facts: Fraudulent charges topped $100k in a single day in some incidents; cumulative up to $1M before access was revoked
UNC6993 generated extra API keys in victim cloud projects to run up >$100k in charges
Attackers exploited LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 to escalate privileges
'LLM Mixer' resale services advertise unlimited-token plans for ~$60/month
Separate grey-market relay reconfigures genuine Codex/Claude Code CLIs to proxy through third-party servers

stories.title: Backporting security fixes at scale with Codex
stories.reason: Trail of Bits' Codex-based backporting pipeline for Patch the Planet is a real running system with concrete throughput numbers, squarely in 'SOC/IR automation' with a primary source -- though the tool itself isn't released, only a public CVE tracker.
key_facts: 149 distinct CVEs backported into stable Linux kernel releases as of Oct 29
Backporting time cut from days to hours per fix; simple backport ~30 min human review, harder one ~3 hours
Fixes also submitted into Fedora and Ubuntu packages
Public artifact is a CVE tracking dashboard (trailofbits.github.io/ptp-linux-stable-cve-dashboard); the tool itself is not released

stories.title: Revolut moves to self-hosted GLM
stories.reason: Revolut replaced frontier-API inference with self-hosted GLM on 56 B200 GPUs at ~$0.30/M tokens (~10x cheaper than Anthropic/OpenAI), citing cost plus GDPR/zero-retention needs -- a concrete, well-sourced data point in the 'how models get served' debate.
key_facts: 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, blended cost ~$0.30 per million tokens
~10x cheaper than prior Anthropic/OpenAI API spend per AI ops lead David Abitbol
Commenters estimate renting that capacity costs $250-300k/month
Compliance (GDPR, zero-data-retention) cited alongside cost as a driver
One commenter reports GLM correctness issues on long context under vLLM

stories.title: AI Vulnerability Finding
stories.reason: Schneier post plus a concrete, checkable data point (PostgreSQL 19 slipping because AI tooling made old bugs much easier to find) -- real evidence that AI bug-finding is changing maintainer workload, not just a vibes claim.
key_facts: Claim: ~3% of all critical bugs in recorded history found in the last month; projected +26% to the all-time total this year
PostgreSQL case: Apr-Sep 2025 had 1,037 master / 724 REL_18_STABLE commits; same window 2026 had 1,443 master / 1,169 REL_19_STABLE commits
Back-patched commits rose >60% year over year, cited as why PG19 is slipping to November
